claims.text: T2DM: consider starting insulin, whatever the other therapy, if hyperglycemia is symptomatic or A1C >10% or glucose ≥300 mg/dL.
claims.quote: In adults with type 2 diabetes, initiation of insulin should be considered regardless of background glucose-lowering therapy or disease duration if symptoms of hyperglycemia are present or when A1C or blood glucose levels are very high (i.e., A1C >10% [>86 mmol/mol] or blood glucose ≥300 mg/dL [≥16.7 mmol/L]).

claims.text: Without severe hyperglycemia, GLP-1–based therapy is preferred to insulin for initial or add-on therapy.
claims.quote: In adults with type 2 diabetes without severe hyperglycemia or hyperglycemic crisis, GLP-1–based therapy is preferred to insulin for initial or add-on glucose-lowering therapy

claims.text: When starting insulin, continue other glucose-lowering agents unless contraindicated or not tolerated.
claims.quote: In adults with type 2 diabetes who are initiating insulin therapy, continue glucose-lowering agents (unless contraindicated or not tolerated)

claims.text: Lispro (Humalog): inject SC within 15 min before a meal or immediately after a meal.
claims.quote: Administer HUMALOG ® U-100 or U-200 by subcutaneous injection into the abdominal wall, thigh, upper arm, or buttocks within 15 minutes before a meal or immediately after a meal.

claims.text: Hypoglycemia is the most common ADR.
claims.quote: Hypoglycemia is the most common adverse reaction associated with insulins, including LANTUS.

claims.text: All insulins shift K+ into cells, possibly causing hypokalemia.
claims.quote: All insulins, including LANTUS, cause a shift in potassium from the extracellular to intracellular space, possibly leading to hypokalemia.

claims.text: Beta-blockers, clonidine: signs of hypoglycemia may be reduced or absent.
claims.quote: Antiadrenergic Drugs ( e.g., beta-blockers, clonidine, guanethidine, and reserpine ): Signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia may be reduced or absent.

claims.text: TZDs: fluid retention and HF; watch for HF and consider reducing or stopping the TZD.
claims.quote: Fluid retention and heart failure with concomitant use of thiazolidinediones (TZDs) : Observe for signs and symptoms of heart failure; consider dosage reduction or discontinuation of TZD if heart failure occurs.

claims.text: Check glucose more often with changes in dose, other drugs, meals or activity, and in renal or hepatic impairment or hypoglycemia unawareness.
claims.quote: Increase frequency of glucose monitoring with changes to: insulin dosage, concomitant drugs, meal pattern, physical activity; and in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and hypoglycemia unawareness.

claims.text: Monitor K+ in patients at risk of hypokalemia.
claims.quote: Monitor potassium levels in patients at risk of hypokalemia and treat if indicated.

claims.text: Learn to recognize and manage hypoglycemia.
claims.quote: Patients and caregivers must be educated to recognize and manage hypoglycemia.
Rotate injection sites to reduce risk of lipodystrophy and localized cutaneous amyloidosis.

claims.text: Don't mix glargine with other insulin.
claims.quote: Do not dilute or mix LANTUS with any other insulin or solution.
Never share a LANTUS SoloStar prefilled pen, insulin syringe, or needle between patients, even if the needle is changed.

claims.text: Check the insulin label before each injection.
claims.quote: instruct patients to always check the insulin label before each injection

claims.text: Severe hypoglycemia can cause seizures and may be life-threatening.
claims.quote: Severe hypoglycemia can cause seizures, may be life-threatening or cause death.

claims.text: Untreated hypokalemia may cause respiratory paralysis, ventricular arrhythmia and death.
claims.quote: Untreated hypokalemia may cause respiratory paralysis, ventricular arrhythmia, and death.
